mechanism_claim: The apparent within-industry stock-selection edge is dominated by co-exposure to industry-group trend continuation; the model's discriminating features (mom_20, ma10/ma20 slopes, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20) are common-momentum proxies that load on the same factor across peer names. The act of 'picking one B0 name inside a hot group' is largely identifying the tightest technical expression of an industry rotation that is already underway, so the PnL should be attributed to industry-timing beta, not firm-level alpha.
evidence_for: All top separating features between selected_winners and false_negatives (mom_20: 0.163 vs 0.058; px_vs_ma50: 0.127 vs 0.056; ma10_slope_5: 0.0268 vs 0.0122; ma20_slope_5: 0.0204 vs 0.0089; up_day_ratio_20: 0.625 vs 0.500; vol_ratio_5_20: 1.424 vs 1.179) are group-coherent momentum/relative-strength features that, by construction, correlate within an industry and are NOT firm-idiosyncratic.

False_negatives with muted stock signals (entity_de1c657364: mom_20=0.058, up_day_ratio=0.65, w4_return_bucket=large_win; entity_535a1beed7: mom_20=0.028, ma20_slope=-0.005, w4_return_bucket=large_win; entity_05b4c6b1f7: mom_20=0.070, up_day_ratio=0.50, w4_return_bucket=large_win) still became winners — indicating the stock-level signal was unnecessary, consistent with industry tailwind doing the work.

False_positive_ruins carried stock-level signals as strong as winners (entity_8f0df3d38e: mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.054, up_day_ratio=0.65, ruin; entity_3472243e0c: mom_20=0.242, ma10_slope=0.030, ruin; entity_4fdc3699fd: ma10_slope=0.091, mom_20=0.185, ruin; entity_b6bcccdf6a: mom_20=0.176, ma10_slope=0.067, ma20_slope=0.045, ruin). If the signals truly isolated firm-level quality, a stock with mom_20>0.17 and positive dual-MA slopes should not have produced an 8-count ruin bucket — implying the stock-level signal provided no protective information.

ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (PIT-observable) is higher for winners (median 0.0300) than false_negatives (0.0195), but this is a breakout-execution feature, not a firm-quality feature — winners entered closer to the group's collective breakout level, again consistent with riding the group move.

The mixed-outcome case entity_6618d3e80c (w4_return_bucket=large_win but also false_positive_ruin) had extreme px_vs_ma50=0.337 and mom_20=0.251 — the W4 win came from the group, and the later ruin came from the firm. This single case cleanly separates the two effects and supports attributing W4 PnL to the group.

Pullback profile of winners (deeper median -15.9%, longer 5.5 weeks) vs false_negatives (-7.3%, 4.0 weeks) indicates the model selects names mid-pullback inside an established uptrend — the textbook signature of group-rotation entries, not idiosyncratic base-breakout timing.
evidence_against: vol_ratio_5_20 separation (1.424 vs 1.179, standardized delta -1.05) is a name-relative-volume feature that can carry some firm-specific information not perfectly shared by the group.

Within any snapshot (e.g., snap_71486ed83c), not every candidate with similar group-level signals is selected (entity_df5478102d and entity_d8e8e7b814 are both rejected false_negatives with moderate mom_20=0.12 and 0.11 respectively), implying some within-group discrimination is occurring.

base_mbox_count is higher for false_negatives than selected_winners (4 vs 3.5), and base_duration_weeks is shorter (44 vs 52) — a count/duration-of-base feature is partially firm-pattern-specific and partially a proxy for cycle phase.

Some winners have very weak technical footprints (entity_8ad5cd4795: ma10_slope=-0.006, ma20_slope=-0.003, mom_20=0.004, up_day_ratio=0.70 → large_win; entity_2f86543bf6: ma10_slope=0.0076, ma20_slope=-0.0078, mom_20=-0.008, up_day_ratio=0.35 → large_win) — if the group were the only driver, such weak technical names should not be disproportionately represented among winners.
falsifiable_predictions: Compute, for each of the 27 cases, the median W4 return of the industry peer set (PIT-defined at snapshot date). The Pearson correlation between stock W4 return and peer-median W4 return should exceed 0.6 across cases; partial correlation holding peer-median W4 constant should drop the apparent selected-vs-not edge to statistical insignificance (bootstrap p>0.10).

A 'buy-every-name-in-top-quintile-industry' naive sleeve, rebalanced at the same snapshot cadence, should capture ≥70% of the selected-sleeve's W4 mean return; if it does, the residual cannot bear a fees+slippage budget for a long-short or factor-pricing premium.

False_positive_ruins should concentrate in snapshots where the industry peer-median W1 return (PIT-observable at entry) is negative or bottom-decile; conversely, false_negatives that became winners should concentrate in snapshots with top-decile peer-median W1 return. A 2x2 contingency test (signal-strength quartile × peer-W1 quartile) should show peer-W1 as the dominant explanatory axis, with signal-strength insignificant conditional on peer-W1.

If the model is rerun with industry-peer-median features included (mom_20, slope, px_vs_ma50 measured on the peer median instead of the stock), the within-sample hit rate on selected_winners should fall below 50% (i.e., the model is learning the group, not the name).

Among snapshots where group momentum is positive but the rejected name has stronger firm signals than the selected name, the rejected name's W4 return should not be statistically lower than the selected name's — falsifying firm-level discrimination.

The 8-count false_positive_ruin bucket should, by W4-end, exhibit peer-median drawdown in 6+ of 8 cases; absence of that pattern (ruins without group drawdowns) would re-favor the within-industry-skill hypothesis.
policy_implications: Do not pay alpha fees for the within-industry sleeve. Capacity, risk budget, and benchmark should be sized against an industry-rotation neutral factor, not a market-neutral long-short; the apparent edge is mostly group beta in disguise.

Add an explicit industry-peer-median W1/W4 PIT feature as a hard pre-filter or position-size scaler. If peer-median is bottom-quartile, the selection signal should be ignored or shorted, since the ruin concentration in strong-signal names confirms strong stock-level signals do not protect against group breakdowns.

Risk management should monitor industry-group drawdown in real time; position-level stops are insufficient because the largest PnL shocks come from correlated peer moves (false_positive_ruins had peer breakdowns despite strong stock signals).

Re-evaluate the false_negatives that became winners (7 cases) as a missed-industry-timing cost, not a missed-stock-picking cost — broadening the candidate set to capture group rotation, rather than tightening the firm-level filter, is the indicated improvement.

If the diagnostic tests above confirm the industry-proxy hypothesis, the 'within-industry advantage' should be reclassified as a known factor exposure (industry momentum / relative rotation) and hedged or beta-priced rather than marketed as security-selection skill.
